title: Suspicious Process Access to LSASS
description: Detects a non-standard process opening LSASS with credential-dumping access rights. Covers common tooling patterns (mimikatz, procdump, comsvcs.dll minidump) while excluding known security products and Windows components.
author: Meruyert
falsepositives: Endpoint protection and EDR agents reading process memory
query: any where winlog.channel:"Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational" and ((event.code:"10" and winlog.event_data.TargetImage:"*\\lsass.exe" and (winlog.event_data.GrantedAccess like~ ("0x1010", "0x1410", "0x1438", "0x143a", "0x1fffff"))) and (not (process.executable.caseless like~ ("*\\MsMpEng.exe", "*\\MpCmdRun.exe", "*\\svchost.exe", "*\\csrss.exe"))))
query_kql: winlog.channel:Microsoft\-Windows\-Sysmon\/Operational AND (winlog.channel:Microsoft\-Windows\-Sysmon\/Operational AND ((event.code:10 AND winlog.event_data.TargetImage:*\\lsass.exe AND (winlog.event_data.GrantedAccess:(0x1010 OR 0x1410 OR 0x1438 OR 0x143a OR 0x1fffff))) AND (NOT (process.executable.caseless:(*\\MsMpEng.exe OR *\\MpCmdRun.exe OR *\\svchost.exe OR *\\csrss.exe)))))

title: Certutil Used to Download or Decode a Payload
description: Detects certutil.exe invoked with urlcache, verifyctl or decode switches. Certutil is a signed Windows binary commonly abused to download or decode attacker tooling while blending in with legitimate administration.
author: Meruyert

title: Cron Job Executing Remote Content
description: Detects cron invoking a shell that pipes remote content into an interpreter. This pattern is a common way to establish recurring access on Linux hosts.
author: Meruyert
falsepositives: Legitimate maintenance jobs that fetch installer scripts

title: PHP File Uploaded to Web Accessible Directory
description: Detects an HTTP POST to a .php path inside a writable or upload directory. A successful upload of executable PHP content is a strong indicator of web shell deployment, the most common way attackers persist on a web server.
author: Meruyert
falsepositives: Applications that legitimately accept PHP file uploads (rare, should be reviewed)
query: any where http.request.method:"POST" and url.path:"*.php" and (url.path like~ ("*/upload*", "*/uploads/*", "*/images/*", "*/tmp/*", "*/files/*"))
query_kql: http.request.method:POST AND url.path:*.php AND (url.path:(*\/upload* OR *\/uploads\/* OR *\/images\/* OR *\/tmp\/* OR *\/files\/*))

title: PowerShell Encoded Command Execution
description: Detects PowerShell or pwsh started with an encoded command switch. Adversaries use base64-encoded commands to obfuscate payloads and evade string-based command line detection.
author: Meruyert
falsepositives: Software deployment tools that wrap scripts in encoded commands (SCCM, Intune)
Administrators running pre-built encoded onboarding scripts
query: any where (process.executable.caseless like~ ("*\\powershell.exe", "*\\pwsh.exe")) and (process.command_line like~ ("* -enc *", "* -encodedcommand *", "* -ec *", "* -e JAB*")) and (not (process.parent.executable.caseless like~ ("*\\ccmexec.exe", "*\\Microsoft.ConfigurationManagement.exe")))
query_kql: (process.executable.caseless:(*\\powershell.exe OR *\\pwsh.exe)) AND (process.command_line:(*\ \-enc\ * OR *\ \-encodedcommand\ * OR *\ \-ec\ * OR *\ \-e\ JAB*)) AND (NOT (process.parent.executable.caseless:(*\\ccmexec.exe OR *\\Microsoft.ConfigurationManagement.exe)))

title: Suspicious Service Installed From User-Writable Path
description: Detects a new Windows service whose binary lives in a user-writable directory or launches through a shell interpreter. This is a common persistence mechanism after initial access.
author: Meruyert
falsepositives: Legitimate software installers that stage files in ProgramData or Temp
Updaters that run a service from a user profile
query: any where winlog.channel:"System" and (event.code:"7045" and (winlog.event_data.ImagePath like~ ("*\\Users\\Public\\*", "*\\AppData\\*", "*\\Temp\\*", "*\\ProgramData\\*", "*cmd.exe /c*", "*powershell*")) and (not (winlog.event_data.ServiceName like~ ("WaaSMedicSvc", "BITS", "WinDefend"))))
query_kql: winlog.channel:System AND (winlog.channel:System AND (event.code:7045 AND (winlog.event_data.ImagePath:(*\\Users\\Public\\* OR *\\AppData\\* OR *\\Temp\\* OR *\\ProgramData\\* OR *cmd.exe\ \/c* OR *powershell*)) AND (NOT (winlog.event_data.ServiceName:(WaaSMedicSvc OR BITS OR WinDefend)))))

title: Windows Defender Real-Time Protection Disabled
description: Detects Windows Defender events indicating real-time protection, behaviour monitoring or tamper protection was disabled. Ransomware and commodity loaders routinely disable Defender before payload execution.
author: Meruyert
falsepositives: Endpoint management tools that temporarily disable protection during upgrades
query: any where winlog.channel:"Microsoft-Windows-Windows Defender/Operational" and (event.code like~ ("5001", "5010", "5012"))
query_kql: winlog.channel:"Microsoft\-Windows\-Windows Defender\/Operational" AND (winlog.channel:"Microsoft\-Windows\-Windows Defender\/Operational" AND (event.code:(5001 OR 5010 OR 5012)))

title: New Local User Account Created
description: Detects useradd creating a new local account, as recorded by the auth log. Attackers create accounts to retain access after the initial vector is closed.
author: Meruyert

title: Scheduled Task Created via Schtasks
description: Detects schtasks.exe creating a new scheduled task from a non-system account. Scheduled tasks are a durable, low-noise persistence and execution mechanism.
author: Meruyert
falsepositives: Software installers and updaters that register scheduled tasks
query: any where process.executable.caseless:"*\\schtasks.exe" and process.command_line:"*/create*" and (not user.name:"*$")

title: Web Request to Common Web Shell Parameter
description: Detects requests carrying command execution parameters frequently used by PHP and JSP web shells (cmd=, exec=, shell=). Complements the upload rule by catching interaction with a shell that was planted earlier.
author: Meruyert
falsepositives: Administrative panels that legitimately use cmd or exec parameters

title: SSH Failed Password Authentication
description: Matches individual failed SSH password attempts. This is intentionally a single-event rule: volume-based escalation (brute force) is handled by the correlation layer in pipeline/correlate.py so the base rule stays portable across SIEMs that do not support threshold aggregations.
author: Meruyert
